newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Britain says Afghan situation still unclear.
newsitem.headline: Britain says Afghan situation still unclear.

text.p: A British minister said on Thursday it was too early to draw any conclusions about the upheaval in Afghanistan.

Liam Fox, Parliamentary Under Secretary of State at Britain's Foreign Office, told a news conference during a visit to Pakistan that London hoped for stability in Afghanistan because of its strategic location.
"We have to wait some time before we see what has happened in Afghanistan. We don't yet have the full extent of the information available to us.

"We will have to look at whether it's going to be a stable government, the country is in fact stable throughout, what sort of government it is and the personalities of the leaders. These are all things which take time to find out," he said.

The European Union has yet to issue any statement on the situation in Afghanistan, where the fundamentalist Islamic Taleban have taken over the capital Kabul and much of the country. The Taleban has since imposed severe restrictions on Afghani women.

Europe's commissioner for humanitarian aid, Emma Bonino, called on Wednesday for the European Union to be more vocal about Afghanistan, particularly reports of human rights abuses since the Taleban captured Kabul on Friday.
Fox declined to comment on the reports.
He is on a tour of South Asian countries, including the Maldives, Sri Lanka and Pakistan.
